This quibble, though, doesn’t in itself completely undermine Johannsen’s case, even if some urgency is reduced and other welfare concerns take higher priority. After all, even if it turned out that populations of wall lizards on balance had net positive experiences, and their lives weren’t terrible, it’s still going to be possible to argue that their experiences could be better. There is still suffering that could be avoided—such as the suffering caused by being predated upon; it could nonetheless be beneficent to help them out. So, there’s still a case for intervention on a beneficence argument. It’s just a weaker case than it would otherwise be.
